scope: Three-lane evidence table (plan Step 7). Each lane of the repository's evaluation discipline - fixed higher prior / documented range / keep current default - is listed with the evidence this survey collected (with source pointers), its gaps, and what the lane would still need. There is NO recommendation column and no lane is endorsed: the decision belongs to the owner and the user, made on this table. Coverage is not justification; none of the evidence below justifies a specific default value.

lane_terms.fixed_higher_prior: Adopt one specific higher AOD550 value as the background-atmosphere default, justified by an independent published value.
lane_terms.documented_range: Replace the point default with a sourced range/distribution (e.g. AOD climatology spread, humidity-variant envelope).
lane_terms.keep_current: Keep the current two-layer OPAC default; the calibration lane (calibrated: presets) plus future independent events carry event-specific values; the standing gap stays explicit.

existing_evidence.evidence: Independent mid-latitude site climatology: GSFC (39.0N) Level-2.0 AOD_500nm median 0.1163 (P25 0.0767, P75 0.2056) over 6677 retrievals in calendar 2011 - specific published values exist in the pool's neighbourhood [0.0259, 0.1839].
Per-site type climatologies report specific means (GSFC urban tau(440) mean 0.24; Lanai clean-marine tau(1020) mean 0.04) that convert to tau(550) inside/near the pool band.

The incumbent OPAC family itself already contains higher members (Table 3 BL types tau(0.55um) up to 0.625 at 80% RH), i.e. a 'higher fixed prior' would be a choice among already-published type values, not a new number.

gaps: The cross-event inversion already showed a single fixed value cannot cover all four events (R=7.110, partially_consistent, criterion preregistered): any fixed prior misfits at least some events by construction.

No collected source reports a value tied to the eclipse observation geometry (grazing low-layer path, 0-10 km, specific latitude/season); site climatologies are vertical-column surface observations, not low-layer-increment analogues.
Every candidate value is heterogeneous in kind (urban vs marine vs clean-continental site climatology); choosing one is a judgement this survey does not make.
what_this_lane_still_needs: Owner+user decision on which specific value and which provenance class (fixed literature prior must stay distinct from calibrated values per AGENTS.md discipline).
Re-run of the counterfactual validation chain with the chosen value (removable-component pattern, exact restoration of the previous state).
Explicit labelling of the resulting misfit per event, and the calibration lane kept separate so the fixed prior is never silently tuned.

existing_evidence.evidence: Site AOD distribution: 71.3% of GSFC 2011 Level-2.0 retrievals fall inside the pool band; the site's dynamic range P90/P10 = 6.97 is the same order as the pool ratio R=7.110 (magnitude comparison only).

The humidity axis is now quantified from the recovered OPAC 1998 component files (26/38 pinned, version-identified): full-axis growth dry->99% RH spans x12.1-x18.6 by component; 50%->99% spans x7.4-x7.6, the same order as R; moderate spans 50->80% x1.5, 50->90% x2.1, 70->98% x3.9-4.0.

Clean-marine low end is documented independently (Lanai tau(1020) 0.01-0.2, mean 0.04), so a documented range can span from clean-marine levels up through urban levels with pinned sources at both ends.
Global vertical/amount context exists (CALIPSO H63 and AOD maps, figure-read approximate).

gaps: Distribution evidence is site/type-conditioned, not eclipse-geometry-conditioned: no source gives an AOD distribution for a 0-10 km grazing-increment layer at the events' latitudes/seasons.
GSFC is one site and one calendar year; robustness across sites/years is not established here (MODIS global product not pursued within the search budget - search_log.md W2.4).

Humidity curves have mid-RH gaps (waso 80/90/95/98, suso 50/90, sscm 70/98/99 not archived anywhere reachable); type-mixture humidity growth is NOT computed (mixtures depend on composition; out of scope for evidence collection).
How a documented range would interact with the calibrated lane (which envelope member applies when) is a design question this survey does not answer.
what_this_lane_still_needs: Owner+user decision on the representation form (which range, which sources anchor its ends, how the default consumes it).

An implementation design consistent with the removable-component pattern (own module, exact zero-value restoration, counterfactual tests) - in particular whether the range replaces the point default or rides alongside it.
Possibly additional sites/years (AERONET multi-site export) and the missing OPAC mid-RH files (would need a reachable mirror or author contact - the latter is outside this task's authorised actions).

existing_evidence.evidence: Clean-atmosphere low values are independently real but rare at mid-latitude sites: GSFC 2011 has 0.2% of retrievals below the pool floor 0.0259 (min 0.0222), and the clean-marine row brackets that level - the June inverted value is at the documented clean tail, not outside all independent observations.

The calibration lane already carries event-specific atmospheres with forced provenance (four calibrated: presets, registry-anchored to the committed inversion product), and the lane-separation discipline is in place.
The standing gap is explicitly documented (brightness closures in the tension band on all four events) - the current default's known limitation is on the record, not hidden.

The humidity axis that was the survey's origin gap is now pinned and quantified, so keeping the current default does not leave the known gap undocumented - the evidence exists for any later lane switch.

gaps: The June floor 0.0259 remains below the OPAC BL-family floor 0.038 (physical_range_exceeded finding stands); no collected source reports values at the envelope floor 0.00259.
The brightness residual stays open under the current default (that is the standing gap itself).
The inverted pool values remain event-calibrated quantities with no independent-prior counterpart at the same geometry.
what_this_lane_still_needs: Nothing further to keep the current default; the queued independent-prediction item (next independent event, e.g. 2028 candidates, tested against calibrated: presets) is the natural continuation and is explicitly outside this task.
If a later lane switch is wanted, the three tables in this survey (coverage matrix, humidity growth, this table) are the evidence base to decide from.

cross_lane_note: Shared gap across all three lanes: no collected source observes the eclipse observation geometry itself (low-grazing 0-10 km column at event latitude/season); every lane would rest on surface-site or satellite column climatologies as analogues. This survey collected evidence only; the lane choice and any default change belong to owner+user.
